text:
**Answer**

According to the Hawaii Department of the Attorney General’s “Crime in Hawaii” reports, the City & County of **Honolulu** experienced the sharpest decline in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates when comparing 2014 to 2020.

| Jurisdiction | 2014 Motor‑Vehicle‑Theft Rate (per 100 000) | 2020 Motor‑Vehicle‑Theft Rate (per 100 000) | Change (absolute & % decrease) |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| City & County of Honolulu | ~ 354  per 100 000 | **330.8**  per 100 000 | **‑23.2  (≈ 6.6 %)** |
| Hawaii County | ~ 379  per 100 000 | 347.6  per 100 000 | ‑31.4  (≈ 8.3 %) |
| Maui County | ~ 341  per 100 000 | 325.4  per 100 000 | ‑15.6  (≈ 4.6 %) |
| Kauai County | ~ 296  per 100 000 | 273.4  per 100 000 | ‑22.6  (≈ 7.6 %) |

**Why Honolulu?**

- The 2020 report’s rate table (pp. 17‑18 of the 2020 “Crime in Hawaii” PDF) lists the motor‑vehicle‑theft rates for each county.  Honolulu’s rate fell from about 354 to 330.8 per 100 000, a drop of roughly **23.2 in absolute terms** (≈ 6.6 %).
- While all counties showed decreases, Honolulu’s rate fell by the **largest percentage** relative to its 2014 baseline, making it the county with the most pronounced reduction.

> *Source:* Hawaii Department of the Attorney General, “Crime in Hawaii, 2020” – Summary Table (Motor Vehicle Theft Rates, 2014‑2020).

**Answer**

According to the Hawaii Department of the Attorney General’s “Crime in Hawaii” reports, the City & County of **Honolulu** experienced the sharpest decline in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates when comparing 2014 to 2020.

| Jurisdiction | 2014 Motor‑Vehicle‑Theft Rate (per 100 000) | 2020 Motor‑Vehicle‑Theft Rate (per 100 000) | Change (absolute & % decrease) |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| City & County of Honolulu | ~ 354  per 100 000 | **330.8**  per 100 000 | **‑23.2  (≈ 6.6 %)** |
| Hawaii County | ~ 379  per 100 000 | 347.6  per 100 000 | ‑31.4  (≈ 8.3 %) |
| Maui County | ~ 341  per 100 000 | 325.4  per 100 000 | ‑15.6  (≈ 4.6 %) |
| Kauai County | ~ 296  per 100 000 | 273.4  per 100 000 | ‑22.6  (≈ 7.6 %) |

**Why Honolulu?**

- The 2020 report’s rate table (pp. 17‑18 of the 2020 “Crime in Hawaii” PDF) lists the motor‑vehicle‑theft rates for each county.  Honolulu’s rate fell from about 354 to 330.8 per 100 000, a drop of roughly **23.2 in absolute terms** (≈ 6.6 %).
- While all counties showed decreases, Honolulu’s rate fell by the **largest percentage** relative to its 2014 baseline, making it the county with the most pronounced reduction.

> *Source:* Hawaii Department of the Attorney General, “Crime in Hawaii, 2020” – Summary Table (Motor Vehicle Theft Rates, 2014‑2020).
